newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open mixed.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open mixed.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were seen opening mixed Monday, with gold and silver firm, but platinum group metals (PGMs) weaker.
Gold benefitted from the weakness in the U.S. dollar, stocks and bonds Friday, but early Monday the dollar was steady and U.S. treasury bonds were recovering a little ground.
COMEX December gold was seen opening unchanged to up 50 cents an ounce from Friday's close of $330.40, after trading a $331.50-330.30 range in overnight ACCESS trade.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $326.85/15 an ounce, compared to the London Monday morning fix at $326.20 and the New York close Friday around $326.90/40.
COMEX warehouse gold stocks slipped 64 ounces to 944,729 ounces Friday, while COMEX silver stocks fell 68,782 ounces to 169,566,068 ounces.
COMEX September silver was seen opening unchanged to up 1.00 cent from Friday's close at $437.50 an ounce.

NYMEX October platinum was expected to open unchanged to down $3.00 an ounce from Friday's close at $443.70 an ounce, while NYMEX September palladium was seen opening unchanged to down $3.00 an ounce also from the previous close at $224.25 an ounce.
In overnight trade, TOCOM platinum prices ended lower, but palladium prices edged higher.
